where: the trailing end of the Missing in action rows — the MISSED count against Call/Text, the ⚠ No parent contact badge, and Elena Petrova's Email row
finding: Folding the row to one line worked, but the whole trailing end is laid out as one right-aligned group of variable width, so the MISSED count rides on whatever contact treatment the row happens to have. That count is the only thing ranking this list — 5, 4, 4, 4 … 3 — and it never appears twice in the same place, so the eye cannot read it as a column and has to re-find it on every row. Elena's row is the worst of the three because it still prints her parent's raw email address beside the Email button: that is the same printed contact string round 2 deleted everywhere else in this card, and it is the string that drags her count 31px out of line while putting a lowercase grey address where nine other rows have a button.
evidence: In dashboard--desktop-full the MISSED chip's left edge is x=683 on the eight Call/Text rows, x=710 on Trevor Boyd's badge row, and x=651 on Elena Petrova's Email row — 59px of spread down ten rows. In the markup the chip sits inside the `min-w-0 flex-1` identity block and the contact group is `lg:shrink-0`, so the chip is positioned by the contact group's width; Elena's group carries `irina.petrova@example.org` after the Email link, the counterpart of the phone number that was removed in r02.
direction: Give the count its own fixed column between the identity block and the contact actions, so ten rows read as one vertical run of numbers with the actions closing the row behind them. And finish the r02 rule while you are there: the printed address should go the way the printed phone number went — the mailto already carries it, and it is what makes one row of ten a different shape from its neighbours.

where: the four stat tiles, specifically the 28rem INCOMPLETE tile against the LAST GATHERING tile
finding: Aligning the tile row's seam to the body seam was right, but it left the row's widths inversely proportional to what the tiles have to say. The fourth cell is more than twice the width of the other three and holds the shortest caption in the row, while the first cell — the only tile carrying a comparison, and the one the round-2 critique singled out as the row's one non-redundant fact — is 30px too narrow for its own caption and wraps it onto a second line, which is what sets the height of all four. So the row reads as three cramped tiles plus a banner, and the tile with the most to say is the one that got squeezed.
evidence: dashboard--desktop-fold: cells at 255–467, 490–701, 724–936, 959–1408 (212/211/212/449px). In the fourth, 'no parent contact' runs 977–1082, leaving 344px of the cell empty; in the first, 'Sunday School · -2 vs 18 before' breaks after 'vs 18' and occupies two lines, 273–418 of 195px available. The grid is `lg:grid-cols-[repeat(3,minmax(0,1fr))_28rem]`.
direction: The seam is worth keeping; the cell assignment is not. Let the tile with the sentence take the wide cell and the bare count take a narrow one, or give the row four equal cells over the left column and leave the right column's width to the cards that actually need 28rem. A cell should be sized by what goes in it, not by which body column it happens to sit above.

where: the 'Next in each series' block in the Upcoming column, against TODAY / NEXT SEVEN DAYS / LATER
finding: Round 2 brought this block's heading down into the group vocabulary, which was right, and that has left the container behind as the only thing making it different from its three siblings. The result is a group that claims the same rank as the others but sits inside a frame nobody else has — and the frame is the same ink-900 as the rows it wraps, so it contributes an extra hairline and no ground. Its cost is alignment: its label and its rows both sit 16px inboard, so the Upcoming column has two left edges and the reader's eye finds a step in a stack that is otherwise flush. The rows inside it are also a different height and lead with a small ✓ where every other row in the column leads with a 44px icon tile, so the block breaks the column's rhythm twice over.
evidence: events--desktop-full: TODAY, NEXT SEVEN DAYS and LATER all start at x=257; NEXT IN EACH SERIES starts at x=273. Row titles are at x=325 in every other group and x=310 inside this one. The section is `rounded-2xl bg-ink-900 ring-1 ring-ink-800` and its `<li>` anchors are `bg-ink-900 … ring-1 ring-ink-800` — identical fill, ring inside ring. Its rows are `min-h-14`, the calendar rows are `min-h-16`.
direction: Now that the heading is a peer, let the block be one: drop the container and let its two rows sit as cards flush with the column like every other group's, so one left edge runs from 'Upcoming' to 'Show later gatherings'. If the box is genuinely wanted to say 'this is maintenance, not calendar', then it needs a ground of its own rather than the same fill with an extra ring — but the cheaper and quieter answer is to let the label do that work.

where: the 'On today' heading block against the 'CATCH UP' heading block
finding: The two sections of this page are labelled three steps apart, and the smaller of the two owns five of the page's six cards. 'Catch up' is set so quietly that it is smaller than the explanatory sentence sitting above it under 'On today' — a section title losing to another section's body copy — and the two sub-lines that do the same job are themselves set at two sizes. Events has just settled this exact pair of ranks (halves at 16px sentence case, groups at 12px uppercase); the sibling screen still runs both idioms for two peers, so the page reads as one titled section followed by an afterthought rather than as two answers to 'which register am I opening'.
evidence: choose-event--desktop-fold: 'On today' renders at ~20px bold ink-50 (bbox 353–453, y 79–97) with a 14px ink-500 sub-line; 'Catch up' at 12px uppercase ink-400 (bbox 353–421, y 395–403) with a 12px sub-line, over five cards. Markup: `h1 text-xl font-bold text-ink-50` + `p text-sm`, versus `h2 text-xs font-bold uppercase tracking-wider text-ink-400` + `p text-xs`. events--desktop-full sets both of its halves at 16px semibold ink-100.
direction: Carry the Events resolution across: one treatment for the page's sections and one size for their sub-lines, with tonight's emphasis carried by the card — which is already brand-ringed and holds the only filled button on the screen — rather than by an eight-point heading gap. If 'On today' is meant to be the page title rather than a section heading, then the first group needs its own label at the same rank as 'Catch up' so the two lists are announced the same way.

where: the sticky control band — quick-add '+', the search field, the Recent / Checked in chips and the All grades chip
finding: Round 2 gave the Students toolbar one control height at pointer sizes and it now sets perfectly; the roster's band, which is the same kind of band, still runs three. The search field is the only control in it that takes the compact pointer step, so it sits 5px shorter than the chips directly beneath it and 9px shorter than the square it is paired with — and because the pair is bottom-aligned, the quick-add square stands 11px proud of the field at the top, which is exactly where the eye reads a mis-set pair. The knock-on is the vertical rhythm: the three control rows are laid out on a consistent 8px gap, but because their contents are different heights the gaps a reader actually sees between adjacent objects run 8, 19, 7, so the header stack looks accidental rather than measured.
evidence: roster--desktop-fold, measured top-to-bottom: '+' 171–220 (50), search field 182–220 (39), Recent/Checked in chips 228–271 (44), All grades 227–272 (46), Change 119–163, event select 120–163. students--desktop-fold, same measurement: header buttons 23–60, search field 117–155, both selects 117–155, both filter chips 118–155 — one height throughout. The roster chips are `min-h-11` with no `pointer-fine` step; the field carries `pointer-fine:py-2`.
direction: One height per band at pointer sizes, the way Students now does it — the chips and the grade control want the same compact step the field already takes, and whatever the quick-add square resolves to should match the field it sits against so the two share a top edge as well as a bottom one. Once the controls agree, the 8px gap between rows will read as the system it already is.
